pr.title: Keep clean on a head a review signed off after the push that queued the label workflow
pr.head: b8dabd2af24735a3705af73e9726cc8491909d1e

summary: Projector marks a pull request whose current head a review signed off with the clean label. In a repository that requires the projector/review commit status, project init also writes a GitHub Actions workflow, .github/workflows/projector-clean.yml, that takes clean off whenever a commit is pushed, because a new head has no review yet.

That workflow decided whether to run from the labels the push event recorded, then removed the label from the pull request as it was when the job ran. A job that ran late, such as one stuck in a queue or re-run later, which replays the old event, could remove clean from a head that a review signed off after the push. Nothing put the label back, because Projector decides sign-off from the review verdicts, so the head never got another review.
The workflow's step now reads the pull request when it runs:

1. The label is already gone. The step exits and changes nothing.
  2. The current head has a success projector/review status. A review signed that head off, so the step keeps the label.
  3. Anything else. The step removes the label, as before.

init used to keep any workflow file that differed from its template, which would have left every repository with the old step. It now recognizes the workflow 0.8.14 wrote by its SHA-256 digest and replaces it, reporting updated, and still keeps a file someone edited.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One Projector review, of b8dabd2, found the head clean and opened no finding thread.
  • It listed one suggestion, about an older window in publish that the job-level if leaves open.
  • The full test suite, project check, and git diff --check pass at the head.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Signed off. The newest Projector verdict on the head is clean and no finding thread is open.
  • projector/review. The commit status publish posts on the reviewed commit, success when signed off, wherever the default branch requires it.
  • Event labels. The labels GitHub records in a pull_request_target event at the moment of the push. A re-run replays them unchanged.

groups.title: The workflow reads the pull request when it runs
groups.kicker: The step that decides whether to take clean off
intro: The template is the file init renders into each repository. Its job still starts only when the push event listed clean, so a push to a pull request without the label starts no runner. The step then makes two API reads with gh api: the pull request's current head and labels, and that head's combined commit status.

The step can only keep or remove the label; only publish adds it. So the step keeps the label wrongly only when the current head has a success status, which publish posts only on a head it signed off.

files.note: The rendered workflow; the step now reads the pull request and the head's status before it edits.

checks.text: This if still reads the event's labels. A push that lands while publish is between reading the head and adding clean records no label, so this job never starts and the new head keeps clean until its own review. That gap is already on main; the review listed it as a suggestion.
The review ran this jq program's input shape against GitHub: the combined-status endpoint returns .statuses[] with .context and .state, one entry per context.
A review that signs the head off between the status read on line 36 and this edit still loses the label. The pull request body names this window, and it lasts the time of one API call.

groups.title: init replaces the earlier release's workflow
groups.kicker: How an existing repository gets the new step
intro: write_clean_workflow runs inside init only after it finds or creates the ruleset that requires projector/review. A file equal to the template is unchanged. A file whose digest matches a workflow an earlier release wrote is replaced and reported updated. Any other file is kept, because someone edited it.
